### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **36** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via getMetaItemLayered (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via resolveWritePackageScope (literal, a string literal in getMetaItemLayered))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ec547fc6611f58f1493daced4978b2b5a95ebf5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f7628f76b3167b488a94ce843e564058e8ee6563` — the merge of head `cd1143c19abc18c2d3005395d9cd1731ea4ebe0f` into base `1ec547fc6611f58f1493daced4978b2b5a95ebf5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f7628f76b3167b488a94ce843e564058e8ee6563 && git checkout f7628f76b3167b488a94ce843e564058e8ee6563
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1ec547fc6611f58f1493daced4978b2b5a95ebf5 cd1143c19abc18c2d3005395d9cd1731ea4ebe0f && git checkout -B drift-repro 1ec547fc6611f58f1493daced4978b2b5a95ebf5 && git merge --no-ff cd1143c19abc18c2d3005395d9cd1731ea4ebe0f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1ec547fc6611f58f1493daced4978b2b5a95ebf5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1ec547fc6611f58f1493daced4978b2b5a95ebf5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `cd1143c19abc18c2d3005395d9cd1731ea4ebe0f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: this card's own diff, `1d8ea4ad7..cd1143c19` (six non-prose paths): packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-face.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-disabled-package-doors.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-disabled-holder-served-stack.test.ts + read as cited code, not reviewed: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-item-reads.ts, protocol-environment-rows.ts, protocol-mutation-fan-out.ts, packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-catalog-echo.ts and packaged-permission-set-lock-gate.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts. The other eight paths the PR's file list still shows are #32501's: they landed on `main` as `c50d10c0` (PR #32808) in a later form and are not this review's.

Read at 2026-11-13T14:39Z. Inputs: card #32354 with every comment (seat ruling 6817756360, epic ruling 6781691009, epic note 6820147040, the dev report 6835365852), the PR body and file list, the diff, and the check-runs on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- C1a, C1b, C1c (widening: a bare read of a name whose only served holder is one enabled package's stored row answers that row, in either save order): right. It is ADR-0150 D3 as seat ruling 6817756360 states it, and `servedRowHolderOf` reads the holders as the ruling words them (registry served holders together with the active rows' bindings, less every disabled package).
- Q2 (two or more served row holders beside a disabled one: `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, `ambiguous-in-environment`, naming only the served holders): right, ruling Q2 A. Q2′ (bare `/layers`, same status, the disabled package no longer named): right.
- C3 (`?package=D`, D disabled and holding the name only as a row, an enabled package shipping it: 404): right as an answer, but it is no longer a move this PR makes. PR #32808 merged as `c50d10c0` before the Version Packages commit `181ad7d4`, so 18.4.0 already answers C3 with 404 through #32501's strict envelope, as this PR's own F1/H2 ablation shows. See ② and S3.
- Not moved, as declared and as the code reads: no installed package disabled (the `getAllPackages` gate returns before any row is read); a name an enabled package ships in code; a name with a package-less row or an environment item.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. No key, value or type an author writes changes.
- Moves the diff makes that the changeset does not list: the in-process layered readers in the Q2 state (S1), an address naming a disabled customization pair (S2), bare `/published` in the Q2 state (S3).

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` with the `!` title, the BREAKING block and `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: the same level and disposition #32808 landed with for the same class of move (a by-name read's answer under a reversible package state). `Check Changeset` is green on this head.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is line-initial in the changeset and the PR body, and still holds: Q2 is a narrowing this PR makes (404 or 200 to 409).
- The changeset's BREAKING headline and its first narrowing bullet state C3 as this release's move. Against `main` today that is false (S3). The changeset says "Every moved answer"; S1, S2 and S3 name answers it leaves out.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on this head: 35 success, 16 skipped, none failed or pending. The PR is `dirty` against `main` (it stacked on #32808's earlier head `1d8ea4ad7`; `main` holds a later form and has since changed `protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` and `protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` for #32568). The merge of `main` is owed before anything else and moves the head: this record does not cover that head. The delta review is this seat's.
- Dev open question 1 (the list cases of epic note 6820147040: keep on this card, or move): no hunk here touches a list door, so `Part of` is the right first line. Whether the card keeps them is the claiming seat's routing call (now `epic:#31527#2`, claim 6855650768), owed before ACCEPT.
- Dev open question 2 (where C3 is declared): option B is gone. #32808's changeset was consumed by 18.4.0 without the bullet. Keep the bullet here, reworded as S3 says.
- Out-of-scope findings in the report: the repeated `(#32622).` in a test comment is a nit, accepted. "Merge main only on a conflict" has come due.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write). File surface: inside claim 6817604765's surface.
- Epic red-line read: owed from the epic seat before ACCEPT, as the claim says. Not this record's.

### ④ Design judgment

`protocol-meta-item-face.ts` (`servedRowHolderOf`, `servedAddressOf`, the plain read's call). The judgment holds against the ruling and the cited code for C1 and Q2. The guards are in the right order: shipped by an enabled package first (ADR-0048 §3.3, so `packagelessContentPackage` keeps judging those names), then the environment item, then the rows, and `rows.unbound` leaves the read as it was. A pair's declared override row of a disabled base is counted as a holder and re-addresses the bare read to the pair, but `readMetaItem` stamps a declared override with the base (`served.overrideOf`), so `isItemOfDisabledPackage` still withholds it: read, not measured, and no pin holds it (N2).

`protocol-exact-qualifier.ts` (`disabledExactAddressHolder`, one line). It does what the ruling asks ("withholds every address naming a disabled package"). It is wider than the changeset says (S2).

`protocol-meta-layered-reads.ts` (two call sites). The re-addressing is right. The refusal path is the problem (S1).

`protocol.ts`: host wiring only. The docblock of `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal`, which the file says is the method's contract, is now wrong in two sentences (S1).

Findings:

- **S1 should-fix.** `servedAddressOf` throws the Q2 refusal, and `getMetaItemLayered` now calls it. The docblock of `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` in `protocol.ts` says the layered ambiguity is "Asked by the DOOR, ⛔ never inside `getMetaItemLayered`: its in-process resolution readers (the security catalog echo, the packaged-permission-set lock gate, `/published`) read the layers of a name with no package and keep the answer they had". After this diff they do not, in the Q2 state:
  - `permission` is a package-scoped read type (`PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`), so `echoSecurityCatalogMutation` (no catch around its `getMetaItemLayered` call) fails inside the awaited mutation projector. `runMutationProjector` turns that into `success: false`, and the catalog keeps its previous echo after a permission-set save. The changeset says "The save door is unchanged".
  - the packaged-permission-set lock gate records a failed layered probe where it read an envelope.
  - `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` now rejects with the Q2 refusal where its signature says it resolves to the refusal or `undefined`. The door's step 1c never sees it anyway, because the door computes the layers first.

  Either keep the ⛔: inside `getMetaItemLayered` a refused judgment leaves the read as it was, and `packagelessLayeredReadRefusal` returns the served-holders refusal for the door's step 1c. Or decide the in-process readers do get the refusal: then rewrite the docblock, declare each reader's moved answer and pin them.
- **S2 should-fix.** The new first line of `disabledExactAddressHolder` returns for every disabled package named. One case moves that the changeset does not list: a customization pair that is disabled while its base is enabled. On `main` such an address is not in `every`, its bases are not all disabled, so the function answers `undefined` and the read serves the base's item (with the pair's declared override, stamped as the base's). On this head it is the pair's withheld 404. The direction agrees with the ruling. Declare it under Narrowing and pin it, with and without an override row, or show a pair cannot be disabled on its own (the disable door admits any writable package, and the pair is writable).
- **S3 should-fix (declarations; do it with the merge of `main`).** Re-measure the FROM column against `main` at the merge and restate C3 in the changeset and the PR body's `Clause-②:` line: 404 since 18.4.0 through #32501's envelope, this change adding a second guard. Take C3 out of the BREAKING headline; Q2 (and S2's pair address, if it stays) is this release's narrowing. Add bare `/published` to the Q2 bullet and pin it on both transports: the door asks the plain read first and answers that read's throw, so in the Q2 state it answers the 409 too, and the Q2 pins read the plain read and `/layers` only.
- **S4 should-fix.** `servedRowHolderOf` counts every active row's binding before the read's own decline rule (`declinesStoredRow`: a shipped flow name's undeclared row, a sealed managed name's row). One declined row beside a disabled shipper re-addresses the read to an address that then serves nothing, which is the same 404. Two would answer the Q2 409 naming two addresses that each serve nothing. Pin the answer for a shipped flow name with rows of two other packages, its shipper disabled, or leave declined rows out of the count.
- **N1 nit.** The plain read passes `request.member` raw; both layered sites pass `resolveBundleMemberSelector(...)`. `overlayMemberValue` trims, so a valid selector reads the same rows. For a blank or misplaced selector on a Q2-state name the 409 is thrown before `readMetaItem`'s `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`. Resolve it once in the face.
- **N2 nit.** No pin for a declared override row of a disabled base at its enabled pair (the paragraph above). One case in the runtime file would hold it.
- **N3 nit.** While any package is disabled, a bare read of a name no enabled package ships reads its active rows twice: once in `servedRowHolderOf`, once in `readMetaItem` (`packagelessAddress` both times; the face does not go through `readItemActiveRows`).

No must-fix. S1 to S4 each earn a delta review of their fix, by this seat, on the head that also carries the merge of `main`.
